measurement: close before print to close after first full session following

names.notes: Reported after close 2026-08-27: non-GAAP EPS $0.70 vs ~$0.58 consensus (+20.7%), revenue $478M (+15% y/y), cloud revenue $235.2M +20% c/c accelerating from 19% in Q4, and FY27 guidance raised. Shares closed the regular session +6.8% into the print, then jumped further after hours and kept climbing through the next full session to close +19.31%, breaking the 12.9% implied move by ~1.5x (falls inside the wide 6.7-27.8% band, but that band is barely informative at this magnitude). The Neutral / No Edge call scores as a miss under the below-expected-move convention (19.31% >> 13.4% unsigned expected) -- exactly the 'stock moved hard and the panel had no view' case, even though the panel's consensus score (-20.7, all seven personas between -15 and -28) leaned bearish and only avoided a Lean Down call by 4.3 points on the threshold. The red-team's specific reversal case -- a repeat of the 2026-05-27 pattern where Elastic beat cleanly and still fell 26% on FY27 guidance implying only ~14.6% growth -- did not fire; this time the guide itself accelerated (cloud growth 19%->20% c/c) and the market treated it as a genuine re-rating, not sell-the-news. The stage-2 preliminary read (-20, bearish) called the wrong direction on the largest move scored so far.

Reported after close 2026-08-27, Affirm's initial FY2027 guide print: revenue $1,165.96M vs ~$1,128.5M consensus (+3.3% beat), a very large headline non-GAAP EPS beat that looks driven by a one-time item rather than the operating trend (the market did not react to it as a clean beat). Shares closed effectively flat, +0.35% close-to-close, well inside the deep-tailed distribution this print normally carries (4 of the last 6 quarters have moved double digits). The Neutral / No Edge call was the honest read of a genuinely split panel (consensus score -0.1, disparity 28.0 -- the widest split of any panelled name to date) and scores as a hit under the below-expected-move convention (0.35% << 10.8% unsigned expected), though the realised move sits below even the low end of the 5.4-22.9% band, so the panel's magnitude sizing was too wide in both directions. The red team's specific reversal case -- a repeat of the 2026-02-05 pattern where Affirm beat and raised guidance but still fell 14.5% on a provision-for-credit-losses jump and a take-rate glide-path guide -- did not fire; the print appears to have landed close enough to expectations on credit/take-rate to avoid either a squeeze or a selloff. The stage-2 preliminary read (-18, bearish) called the wrong sign on what is functionally a noise-level move -- the same 'near-zero move, prelim called a direction anyway' pattern seen on BILL (2026-08-19).
